method: Independently re-fetched via the in-app browser against the first-party host (WebFetch returns HTTP 403 on www.sap.com/design-system, reconfirmed this run). Content retrieved through the CMS raw-content variant <page>.plain.html on the canonical origin https://sap.com (www.sap.com redirects there). Every evidence_quote was tested by exact normalized substring match in JS - HTML stripped, entities decoded, curly quotes/dashes normalized, whitespace collapsed, and whitespace-before-punctuation introduced by inline hyperlinks removed. No quote was matched by eye or by memory.

ip_review.theme_hex_values: NONE. Regex scan of the whole lane file for #RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA and rgb()/rgba() returned no matches. The lane deliberately excluded theming and design tokens, and that exclusion holds under scan.
ip_review.asset_urls: NONE. Scan for sap.com asset paths (.svg/.png/.jpg/.webp/.woff) and CMS media_<hash> identifiers returned no matches. Note: the live source pages DO serve media_<hash>.svg assets, so this was a real exposure that the lane avoided.
ip_review.verbatim_quote_length: PASS. Longest evidence_quote is 15 words; zero records exceed the 15-word ceiling. Records at the 15-word limit include R08-001, R08-004, R08-006, R08-010, R08-014, R08-031, R08-034, R08-057, R08-088, R08-094. These sit exactly at the boundary - if the ceiling is ever tightened, they are the ones that break first.
ip_review.trademark_flags: Two records self-flagged ip_risk=TRADEMARK: R08-011 (shell bar) and R08-015 (launchpad shell). Both describe SAP-branded shell surfaces. The flags are appropriate and should be honoured downstream - describe the structural pattern, do not reproduce SAP naming or branding in the delivered Zoho UI.
ip_review.residual_risk: The real remaining risk is not in the quotes but in the behaviour_description fields, which paraphrase SAP guideline prose at length and in guideline voice. They are paraphrase rather than verbatim copying, but they should be rewritten into the project idiom before shipping in a client deliverable rather than pasted through.

results.replacement_quote: A floorplan is the UI layout consisting of patterns and components, usually describing the content of the full page.
results.what_source_actually_says: The page defines the floorplan correctly, but it is a catalogue of design-system CONTENT CATEGORIES (Design Tokens, Themes, Design System Assets, Components, Patterns, Floorplans, Templates, Design Specifications), not a compositional hierarchy. Critically, 'Templates' on this page is defined as 'any template used for marketing and communications content, for example a PowerPoint template or a solution brief' - a marketing artifact, NOT a UI layer sitting above floorplans.
results.notes: Quote matched verbatim. Narrower true statement: a floorplan is the UI layout consisting of patterns and components, usually describing the full page. The claim's added positioning - 'sitting above components and below templates in the system hierarchy' - misreads the article's list order as a hierarchy and misreads 'Templates' as a UI-composition level. Drop the hierarchy clause; keep the definition.

results.replacement_quote: With SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar
results.what_source_actually_says: The cited page is an SAP Fiori ELEMENTS framework article. Its full text reads: 'With SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar and shares many features and settings with the list report...' It then gives only a feature-availability table (view management, header title, filter bar unavailable, table title with row count, growing table, search in table toolbar, personalization, export). The words 'comparably small', 'one by one', and 'predefined' appear NOWHERE on this page. The page itself defers design intent elsewhere: 'For design information, see the Worklist Floorplan guidelines' - the article the lane's own gaps note proves is absent from the published index.
results.notes: TWO problems. (1) SCOPE: the source states a framework-specific behaviour ('With SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is...'); the claim generalises it into a floorplan-wide definition. (2) UNSOURCED ADDITIONS: 'processing a predefined, comparably small set of items one by one' is not on this page. 'Predefined set of objects' is sourced, but from a DIFFERENT page (when-to-use-which-floorplan, the source of R08-051). 'Comparably small' and 'one by one' are supported by NEITHER page. Narrower true statement: in SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar; per when-to-use-which-floorplan it is for processing a predefined set of objects where a filter bar is not needed and predefined views are possible. Load this claim into the blueprint WITHOUT any size ceiling.
